elements.content: Grammar focus: Hedging & Diplomatic Stance.

Hedges sit at the edge of a claim: an adverb before the adjective (arguably the best), a reporting verb in the conditional (we would suggest), or a concessive opener (admittedly, to be fair). They do not remove the claim; they set its strength.

arguably — marks a claim as debatable: arguably the safest option
admittedly — concedes a point: admittedly, the data is thin
to a certain extent — limits the scope: to a certain extent, you are right
it would appear that — reports without asserting: it would appear that the costs rose
we would suggest — recommends without ordering: we would suggest a later date
there may be a case for — opens a possibility: there may be a case for postponing
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence is properly hedged?
options: The results are arguably weaker than the baseline.
The results are disappointing, to say the least.

elements.content: 2. Admittedly signals that the speaker is...
3. Which is the weakest commitment?
options: We would suggest revisiting the deadline.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

Admittedly — the rollout was rushed, and the results show it. (Concede first, then argue.)
The proposal is arguably — the safest of the three, though the cost is real. (Commit less, invite debate.)
We would suggest that — the deadline be revisited in June. (Recommendation without an order.)
What do you observe?

The claim still has content, but the speaker leaves room for the other side. Admittedly concedes a point before disagreeing; arguably marks a position as debatable; to a certain extent limits how far the speaker goes.
1. What does admittedly do at the start of a sentence?
options: It concedes a point before the speaker disagrees.
It strengthens the claim that follows.

elements.content: 2. Which hedge limits the scope of an agreement?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: Can present research findings, formulate empirical hypotheses, and hedge academic conclusions responsibly

Success criteria:
- I can concede a point before disagreeing.
- I can mark a claim as debatable without weakening it to nothing.
- I can recommend a course of action without giving an order.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ The policy is a disaster (no hedge in a formal report) → ✅ The policy has arguably produced worse outcomes than intended
❌ I think you are wrong (flat contradiction) → ✅ I would take a different view on that point
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

Admittedly, the schedule slipped twice.
To a certain extent, the criticism is fair.
One might argue that the opposite is true.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where distancing passive reporting carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Distancing Passive Reporting. Use the impersonal form when the claim itself is the topic: It is alleged that funds were moved. Use the personal form when the person is the topic and the claim is background: He
